package_info.package_versions: 8.0.1 (and any version published under these names)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are copycat versions of the legitimate 'mitmproxy' library, but with critical security safeguards deliberately removed from the web API. Specifically, they disable CORS protections and the X-Frame-Options header, introducing an artificial remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability. This allows any user on the same network to execute arbitrary code on the host running the mitmproxy web interface. The packages are designed to appear as legitimate or newer versions, increasing the risk of accidental adoption by unsuspecting developers.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the mitmproxy web interface is started

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sets the Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Headers, and Access-Control-Allow-Methods headers to '*', allowing any origin to send requests with any headers and methods to the mitmproxy web API, resulting in unauthenticated remote code execution by any network peer.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Setting CORS headers to '*' on a sensitive API endpoint exposes the application to cross-origin requests from any source, enabling attackers to interact with the API without authentication and potentially execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate mitmproxy installations restrict API access to trusted origins and authenticated users. The malicious code removes these safeguards, allowing unrestricted access from any origin and enabling exploitation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Open CORS headers may be used for public, read-only APIs with no sensitive operations, but never for APIs capable of code execution or administrative actions.
key_indicators: Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to '*' on a sensitive API endpoint
Access-Control-Allow-Methods includes POST and DELETE without authentication or origin restriction

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the mitmproxy web interface is started

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code comments out the X-Frame-Options header, allowing the web interface to be embedded in iframes, which enables clickjacking attacks and increases the risk of further exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling the X-Frame-Options header on an administrative interface allows the web interface to be embedded in iframes, making it vulnerable to clickjacking attacks that can trick users into performing unintended actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard security practice is to set X-Frame-Options to 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN' for admin interfaces to prevent framing. Commenting out this header removes a critical security control.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some public-facing sites may allow framing for embedding content, but this is never appropriate for sensitive admin APIs or interfaces with code execution capabilities.
key_indicators: X-Frame-Options header explicitly commented out in code
Administrative web interface lacks anti-clickjacking headers

attack_chain.action: User installs and runs the malicious mitmproxy2 or mitmproxy-iframe package, believing it to be a legitimate or newer version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Web interface is started with weakened security controls.

attack_chain.action: The web API is exposed with all CORS protections disabled and the X-Frame-Options header removed, making the API accessible from any origin and embeddable in iframes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Any user on the same network can send arbitrary requests to the API.

attack_chain.action: An attacker on the same network sends a crafted HTTP request to the exposed API, exploiting the lack of authentication and CORS protections to trigger remote code execution on the victim's machine.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution on the victim's system.

behavioral_signatures: mitmproxy web interface responds with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
mitmproxy web interface missing X-Frame-Options header
Unrestricted CORS headers present on sensitive local web APIs
mitmproxy web interface accessible from non-local origins without authentication
file_indicators: mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py with commented out or missing X-Frame-Options header
mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py with Access-Control-Allow-Headers: '*' and Access-Control-Allow-Methods including POST, DELETE
network_indicators: mitmproxy web interface accessible from any origin on the local network
Unusual POST or DELETE requests to mitmproxy API endpoints from non-local or unauthenticated sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mitmproxy installations where the web interface responds with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and lacks the X-Frame-Options header. Scan dependency manifests for package names 'mitmproxy2' or 'mitmproxy-iframe'. Review mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py for commented out or missing security headers. Alert on any mitmproxy API endpoints that accept unauthenticated requests from non-local origins or allow POST/DELETE methods without authentication.
